newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Political worries drag down Paris stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Political worries drag down Paris stocks.

text.p: French stocks were dragged down sharply by an attack of political jitters on Friday and German shares were knocked back by a weaker dollar which dimmed export prospects.
The Paris bourse dropped over two percent because of worries over a rumoured snap election. Frankfurt ended the day down over one percent although after-hours trade looked healthier.
The dollar slipped nearly a pfennig after the German central bank President Hans Tietmeyer's comments that the Bundesbank was not interested in seeing the mark weaken further.

The big fall in the French CAC 40 index came after President Jacques Chirac failed to calm rumours about a snap election or cabinet reshuffle, and the opposition Socialist party said it was ready to contest a vote.

The Socialists have accused Chirac of considering parliamentary elections a year early to renew the centre-right majority before a new bout of austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency.
"The main concern remains the possibility of early elections in parliament but there is no panic yet," one broker said.

The market was likely to remain volatile over the next few days as investors wait to see if the French parliament is dissolved, brokers said. "We might get more action on Monday when some players return from their holidays," one said.

Some investors were worried that the dissolution of parliament might pave the way for a new austerity plan in France ahead of the euro single currency, another broker said. "There is some concern over a new austerity plan and its possible impact on economic growth," one broker said.
In Frankfurt, floor trade ended down by 1.2 percent because of the falling dollar but computerised dealing on the IBIS index perked up, perhaps encouraged by a robust start on Wall Street.
But volumes were thin and there was unease about the volatility on Wall Street, frequently a strong influence on European bourses.
"Nobody is trusting the gains on Wall Street anymore," said one trader, noting widespread expectations of a further U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase in May.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was the best performer, edging into the plus column after Wall Street opened with gains of 0.3 percent, led by high-tech stocks after a better-than-expected results by Microsoft.
But many of the big institutions steered clear of the market because of pre-election nerves and fears of rising interest rates.
Shares in British Telecommunications Plc firmed 7-1/2p to 450 at one point after news of a global alliance with its merger partner MCI Communications and Telefonica de Espana.
On currency markets, the dollar fell in slow trade against the mark and was weaker on the yen by mid-afternoon, its energy sapped by dollar-dampening comments out of Japan and Germany.

Traders said an absence of economic data from the United States and Germany was making European trade lethargic, adding that the approach of the weekend and a G7 finance ministers' meeting next week was adding to the reluctance to stir up the market.
The dollar lost nearly a pfennig because of Teitmeyer's remarks.

Against the yen, the dollar was a bit stronger after slipping earlier after remarks made overnight by Eisuke Sakakibara, the influential head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's international finance bureau.

Sakakibara, in an interview with Reuters, warned of the danger of assuming Japan would not raise interest rates within the next year. It would be natural for the Bank of Japan to raise rates when the strength of the economy was confirmed.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7155 marks and 125.90 yen after ending at 1.7241 and 125.97 in late trading in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 7.5 points at 4,306.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 69.06 points at 2,546.12.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 38.86 points at 3,344.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.10 versus $343.15 at the close in London on Thursday. Silver was three cents lower at $4.73.
